This is affecting several critical workflows.

Evan

Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx + timeouts across /v1/generate (prod)

Evan — we pulled the traces in the console. Early findings: a new autoscaling kernel change that rolled at 08:30 PT increased KV cache churn under Platmore's request size profile. That combined with aggressive client retries produced contention and temporary request backlog leading to 503s and 429s.

Mitigations applied at 09:05 PT:
- Rolled back kernel selectors to the previous stable build
- Enabled an emergency per-customer soft-rate limit to shed retries
- Short-circuited prefix-caching for Platmore's most frequent endpoint to reduce KV eviction churn

Status at 09:40 PT: error rate down to baseline but latency elevated for ~20 more minutes as KV warmed. We're collecting a full outage window and token counts for SLA calculation.

Rishi
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx + timeouts across /v1/generate (prod)

Evan — thank you for the context and for negotiating in good faith while we completed the post-incident review. Summary and resolution: 

- Root cause: autoscaling kernel rollout increased KV cache churn triggering a retry-amplified backlog for Platmore's request profile. Rollback and targeted cache changes fixed the issue; system returned to baseline within ~30 minutes of mitigations.
- Affected window: 2026-06-15T08:35:00-07:00 through 2026-06-15T09:10:00-07:00 (UTC-7)
- Measured: ~1.18M attempted tokens; elevated error rate averaging 17.9% during the window
- Proposed remediation & follow-up:
  - Engineering: permanent change to kernel rollout gating for high-client-throughput customers and added pre-deploy canary testing for KV churn on large-request profiles (ETA: 3 weeks)
  - Ops: per-customer early-shedding policy and a retry-smoothing advice doc for clients (ETA: 2 weeks)
  - CS: runbook and monitoring hook for Platmore to get immediate notification on regressions

Credit proposal (final): Redwood will apply a one-time 20% credit on Platmore's June inference usage invoice. Rationale: balances measured impact, mitigating actions already taken, and precedence for severity class B incidents. If Platmore prefers an alternate formulation (flat token refund), we can process that as well; both are documented in the attached credit breakdown.

If this is acceptable, we'll prepare a formal credit note and a brief executive approval email. Thanks again for the patient coordination — looking forward to closing out.

Hannah
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: credit-breakdown-platmore-6-19.pdf
